steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Was that another trick of the shadows? This isn't the right way. I'm going in circles.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I can't see the sky. How long has it been...? How far do I still have to go?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Well, I'm in the Dark Woods, at least. The mist and noise Brigid was talking about didn't keep me out.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Tricky fae, shadows pointing the wrong way, fowlbeasts that trip you with branches... That's all more or less the same as when I was bringing Moran and the others back.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The trees are too tall, and the leaves too thick. They block out the sky, making the life here different from outside.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...This is the right path. I'm at the heart of the Dark Woods now.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The scenery seems different from before. Where did the red and gold of autumn go?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Why does it look like this?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The black mist?!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So the woods are rejecting me after all?
Loughshinny grabs her weapon tightly. If Nemos was right, and Dublinn never returned after leaving the city, then they were most likely swallowed by the mist.
But it shows no sign of aggression. It simply lingers.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Does it... reject me?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, it's closer to indifference... disappointment?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Why?
There is no answer except the rustling of leaves.
Loughshinny shakes her head and cautiously goes around the mist, choosing a path that looks like it has a light at the end. The mist remains indifferent to her passage.
The fae that delight in leading travelers astray are nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Another dead end...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No time to waste here. I'm sorry, but I'll have to burn a way through—
You're overthinking it.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Take a guess.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You... how could it be?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You're that gentleman from the city... I wanted to ask you something, but you—

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Indeed, hardly the most amicable of partings. Since then, I've been following and watching you for a while now. Consider it my way of reflecting on myself.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: I'll admit you're not quite what I thought. But this is no time for small talk.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Do not burn the trees. It should be enough to illuminate them with your fire. See for yourself what they really are.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: 'What they really are'...?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The leaves are razor sharp. The brambles are hard, and the branches have a metallic gleam... what is this?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: That's not important. What's important is that your fire can't burn through it.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Now follow me.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Hurry, before the black mist changes its mind!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: We can talk later, but if that thing is in a bad mood, there won't be anything left to bury when it's done with you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Isn't that a dead end?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Why do you put so much faith in what you see?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Just listen and move!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This is... the path I took when we came to Na Saoirsí!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So this is where those trails lead?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If you don't mind me asking, are you and the forest fae—

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Don't be ridiculous. I have nothing to do with them.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: The woods, though... Centuries have passed, but it's hardly changed at all, other than the black mist.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Ruins the view, really.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We'll be out of the Dark Woods soon. Now could you—

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Tsk, tsk, this is really...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What's happening?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Look behind you.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Reed!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Reed! We're here!
The refugees appear on the well-lit edge of the woods.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: What happened in the city? It's like the black mist got angry the moment you entered it, cutting it off from the outside. It's been days since anyone went into the Dark Woods.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: A few people were hunting on the outskirts when they heard sounds from within, and saw what looked like fire.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Whenever something similar happened before, the wakemen told us not to approach the woods.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: This time, though, we recognized your fire. We could hardly ignore it.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You shouldn't have come. It's dangerous here—

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Then you shouldn't have either, not on your own. We all learned our lesson about letting you go off alone after waiting for you in the marshes outside Londinium.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: We trust you. So please, trust us back.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: You're welcome. Let's go back to camp.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Sir, would you—

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Who are you talking to? Is there someone else with you?
The red dragon turns around, but her uninvited companion has already vanished without a trace, like the dew under the morning sun.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Thank you for providing refuge for these people.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Nemos entrusted them to us. We simply did our part.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: On behalf of the wakemen, I promise that we will not reveal your existence to anyone unaware. And you have seen with your own eyes that your people are safe. Now it is time for you to leave.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: What do you mean? Is she not welcome here?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Neither are your people, Moran.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Whenever two red dragons meet, endless conflict awaits. If you insist on involving yourselves in it, then we can no longer offer you sanctuary.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: How could you?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: This is how we have always been. The wakemen neither start nor end conflicts.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: The disputes of the living are not our concern. We watch over only the souls of the departed.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: If you are truly the noble and compassionate leader Moran imagines you to be, you will not drag these innocents into your battle, red dragon.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This isn't a battle between two red dragons. I came to seek your help on behalf of the people of Na Saoirsí—

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Every battle has its reasons.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: It's not an excuse. Reed wouldn't do that.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Excuse or not, the disputes of the living are none of our concern... A hard-learned lesson whose bitter fruits we continue to taste to this day.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Now leave.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What if I'm here to ask you to hold a funeral?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: A funeral?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: In that case, the wakemen will welcome you. But for that, and only that.

spans.text: case, the wakemen will welcome you. But for that, and only that.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Now tell me the name of the departed, their deeds in life, and... present the remains.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: His name was... Culann. He was a blacksmith.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Culann?!

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: How did he die?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The purple flames of death took both his life and his will. Not even my flames can help him now.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Then why is it that not a single denizen of Na Saoirsí has come to us to request a funeral since the city became independent?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: So it transpires that the first Na Saoirsían to be mourned since the end of the war was not taken by war at all.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So I weave the straw into a ring like this?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Yes. Then adorn it with these flowers, and the wreath is complete.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I remember when the farmers put a wreath on your head, praying for a good harvest next year.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Mhm.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Feels like old times. I miss that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Are you not happy here?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I rather enjoy it myself, but the others might find it stifling.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: The life of a wakeman is almost like a self-punishment, after all. What's the word for it again? 'Asceticism'?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: No alcohol, no overeating, no fancy foods—can't even laugh too loud. They wake up before sunrise and sleep after midnight, and everything in between is some ritual or other.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: At least they don't expect the same from us, but there's no avoiding them when we have to help out on the farms and stuff.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: I've practically forgotten how to laugh—hah.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Moran's the only one who goes out of her way to talk to them. She's learning something new every day. Might be how they tie certain knots, might be how to estimate the age of a tree.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Compared to the wakemen in the tales, though...

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Your Highness?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Ma'am.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: I did not expect to find you here working with them.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Reed has always been like this.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Should we excuse ourselves?

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: No, I simply came to confirm the facts of the departed's life, for the purpose of the ritual.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Please, tell me. What happened to Culann?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I will tell you all that I saw, as I saw it.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I hope it makes you feel something.
